overviewHtml:
This ungraded knowledge check assesses your understanding of the dispute over training AI models on copyrighted work. You'll be asked about the creators' and developers' positions, the three US rulings, the Copyright Office report and the UK ruling, and licensing, settlements, and market dilution.

Note: Use this to test yourself, review the feedback on any questions you miss, and retry until you feel confident before moving forward.

forms.stemHtml: A developer argues that training a model on books is a fair use because the model does a different job from the books and doesn't replace them. Which idea is this argument built on?

options.html: Market dilution
options.text: Market dilution
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Market dilution is the creators' concern that AI-generated works will weaken the market for human work. The developer's argument is built on transformative use.

options.html: Transformative use
options.text: Transformative use
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! A transformative use gives a copied work a new purpose or character instead of substituting for the original.

options.html: Collective licensing
options.text: Collective licensing
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Licensing is the remedy creators propose. The developer's argument is built on transformative use.

options.html: Infringing copy
options.text: Infringing copy
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. An infringing copy is a term from the UK case about whether a model is itself a copy. The developer's argument is built on transformative use.

forms.stemHtml: In Bartz v. Anthropic (2025), how did the court treat the company's library of pirated books?

options.html: As fair use, because the books were later used for training
options.text: As fair use, because the books were later used for training
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. The court held that training was a fair use and that keeping pirated copies in a central library was not, and it ordered a trial on those copies.

options.html: As outside the case, because no author objected to it
options.text: As outside the case, because no author objected to it
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. The pirated copies were central to the case. The court held they were not a fair use and ordered a trial on them.

options.html: As fair use, because the company also bought print copies
options.text: As fair use, because the company also bought print copies
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Scanning purchased books was held to be fair use. Keeping pirated copies was not, and the court ordered a trial on them.

options.html: As not a fair use, with a trial ordered on those copies
options.text: As not a fair use, with a trial ordered on those copies
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! The judge held that the company had no entitlement to use pirated copies for its central library, even though he found the training itself to be fair use.

forms.stemHtml: In Kadrey v. Meta (2025), the judge ruled for Meta on the claim about training. What did he say the ruling stands for?

options.html: That these authors argued wrongly and lacked evidence
options.text: That these authors argued wrongly and lacked evidence
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! He wrote that the ruling stands only for the proposition that the plaintiffs made the wrong arguments and failed to develop a record in support of the right one.

options.html: That training models on copyrighted books is lawful in general
options.text: That training models on copyrighted books is lawful in general
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. The judge wrote that the ruling does not stand for that. It stands only for the point that these authors argued wrongly and lacked evidence.

options.html: That authors can never show harm to the market for their books
options.text: That authors can never show harm to the market for their books
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. The judge called market dilution a potentially winning argument. The ruling stands only for the point that these authors argued wrongly and lacked evidence.

options.html: That every author whose book Meta used has lost the right to sue
options.text: That every author whose book Meta used has lost the right to sue
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. The ruling affects only the thirteen authors who sued. It stands only for the point that these authors argued wrongly and lacked evidence.

forms.stemHtml: In Getty Images v. Stability AI (UK, 2025), why did the court not decide whether training the image model on Getty's photographs infringed copyright?

options.html: The court held that UK law has no rules about photographs
options.text: The court held that UK law has no rules about photographs
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. UK copyright law covers photographs. Getty dropped the training claim because there was no evidence the training took place in the UK.

options.html: Stability AI admitted the claim before the trial began
options.text: Stability AI admitted the claim before the trial began
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. There was no such admission. Getty dropped the training claim because there was no evidence the training took place in the UK.

options.html: Getty dropped the claim for lack of evidence of UK training
options.text: Getty dropped the claim for lack of evidence of UK training
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Getty acknowledged there was no evidence that training and development took place in the United Kingdom, and UK copyright law covers acts done in the UK.

options.html: The judge ruled that training is always a fair use in the UK
options.text: The judge ruled that training is always a fair use in the UK
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. The court made no ruling on training, and the UK has no general fair use defense. Getty dropped the training claim because there was no evidence the training took place in the UK.

forms.stemHtml: Which statements about the 1.5 billion dollar settlement in Bartz v. Anthropic are accurate? (Select all that apply.)

options.html: It covers the company's past copying of the listed works
options.text: It covers the company's past copying of the listed works
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! It addresses past acquisition and copying, through August 25, 2025.

options.html: It establishes that training on books is unlawful
options.text: It establishes that training on books is unlawful
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. A settlement is an agreement and sets no precedent. The court's ruling that training was a fair use was left in place.

options.html: It leaves open claims about what the models produce
options.text: It leaves open claims about what the models produce
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Claims based on the models' outputs are not released.

options.html: It leaves open claims about future conduct
options.text: It leaves open claims about future conduct
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Authors keep their rights over anything the company does later.

title: Copyright, training data, and creative work
